texts: Welcome to Quiz Rush! Forty questions, four levels, ten seconds each. Grab a pen, keep your score, and let's go!
Let's warm up! Which city is home to this famous tower?
Paris! Completed in 1889 for the World's Fair.
Cute one coming up. What is this animal?
A giant panda! Wild pandas live in the mountains of central China.
Look up at the sky. Which planet is this?
That's Saturn, and its rings are made mostly of ice.
Ancient wonder alert! In which country are these pyramids?
Egypt! The Great Pyramid is over four thousand five hundred years old.
Big city lights. What is the capital of Japan?
Tokyo, of course. It hosted the Summer Olympics in 1964 and 2021.
Sports fans, this one's yours. How many players per team are on the court in basketball?
Five players per team. The game was invented in 1891.
Deep breath. What is the largest ocean on Earth?
The mighty Pacific, covering about one third of our planet.
Picture this bridge. Which city is it famous for?
San Francisco! The Golden Gate opened in 1937.
Think about the map. How many continents are usually counted?
Seven continents, and Asia is the biggest of them all.
Last easy one! Which gas do plants absorb from the air?
Carbon dioxide. Plants turn it into sugar using sunlight.
Level up! Welcome to the Medium round. In which country is this ancient site?
Peru! The Inca built Machu Picchu in the fifteenth century.
Careful, this one tricks a lot of people. What is the capital of Australia?
Not Sydney... it's Canberra! Chosen as the capital in 1908.
Shiny question! What is the hardest natural material?
Diamond, pure carbon and incredibly tough.
Let's head to Africa. Which is the longest river on the continent?
The Nile, flowing all the way north to the Mediterranean.
A monument to love. In which country is it?
India! The Taj Mahal was built by Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife.
Kick-off time! How many players does a soccer team have on the field?
Eleven, and that includes the goalkeeper.
Chemistry class! What is the chemical symbol for gold?
A U! It comes from the Latin word aurum.
Ready, set, run! What is the fastest land animal?
The cheetah, hitting around one hundred kilometres per hour in short bursts.
Those white sails are iconic. In which country is this opera house?
Australia! The Sydney Opera House opened in 1973.
Final Medium question. What is the largest planet in our solar system?
Jupiter. You could fit more than a thousand Earths inside it.
You made it to the Hard round! In which country is this ancient city?
Jordan! Petra was carved straight into the rock by the Nabataeans.
Small step, giant leap. In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
Nineteen sixty-nine. Apollo 11 touched down on July twentieth.
Think tiny. What is the smallest country in the world?
Vatican City, less than half a square kilometre.
Snow at the equator? In which country is this mountain?
Tanzania! Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa.
Not the biggest city! What is the capital of Canada?
Ottawa, sitting right between Ontario and Quebec.
Your body knows this one. How many bones are in the adult human body?
Two hundred and six. Babies start with around three hundred!
A famous gift. Which country gave this statue to the United States?
France! The statue was dedicated in 1886.
Back to the periodic table. Which element has the symbol F E?
Iron! F E comes from the Latin word ferrum.
Gladiators, get ready! In which city is this ancient arena?
Rome! The Colosseum was completed in the year eighty.
Last Hard question. What is the largest hot desert in the world?
The Sahara, almost as big as the United States.
This is it, the Genius round! Which country has the most lakes?
Canada, home to more than half of the world's lakes.
Only true geography experts know this. What is the capital of Mongolia?
Ulaanbaatar, the coldest national capital on Earth.
A weird one from space. Which planet rotates on its side?
Uranus, tilted by about ninety-eight degrees.
Sunrise over a legend. In which country is this temple?
Cambodia! Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world.
Wings out! Which is the only mammal capable of true flight?
The bat. Flying squirrels and sugar gliders only glide.
Back to where it all started. Which city hosted the first modern Olympic Games?
Athens, in 1896, right in this very stadium.
Listen closely. Which language has the most native speakers?
Mandarin Chinese, with close to a billion native speakers.
How deep can you go? What is the deepest lake in the world?
Lake Baikal in Siberia, more than one thousand six hundred metres deep.
Almost there! What is the capital of New Zealand?
Wellington, the southernmost capital in the world.
Final question! How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
About eight minutes. That's one hundred and fifty million kilometres!
That's the end of the rush! So, what's your score? Drop it in the comments, and subscribe for the next quiz. See you soon!
